extracted.intended_audience: EU Commission staff (lead DGs, policy officers, better-regulation teams) responsible for planning and conducting stakeholder consultations, impact assessments, evaluations and fitness checks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, running and using stakeholder consultations and evaluations in the context of EU Commission policy-making (including impact assessments and fitness checks). Covers principles, minimum standards, timeframes, methods, documentation and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take an inclusive approach by consulting as widely as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult broadly and transparently among stakeholders to seek a whole spectrum of views and avoid bias or regulatory capture. Map and identify relevant stakeholder categories and ensure opportunities for all interested parties to express opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and accountability (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the consultation process and how it has affected policymaking transparent to those involved and to the general public, including to persons with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish consultation documents, contributions and results; provide factual summaries and synopsis reports explaining how input was considered; ensure accessibility (including for persons with disabilities); include privacy statements covering data handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult at a time when stakeholder views can still make a difference, taking account of proportionality and specific restraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan consultations early enough in policy development so input can influence outcomes; choose methods appropriate to objectives and timing; avoid late consultations that cannot affect decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the consistency (across all services) of consultation processes, analysis, review and quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate consultation strategies across DGs and services; use interservice groups; apply consistent standards, analysis and quality checks to consultation outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (minimum standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: All consultation documents should be clear and concise and include all necessary information to facilitate responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questionnaires are very technical, include a set of more general questions for non-specialists; consider using editing/translation services; test documents with groups resembling target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting (minimum standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the consultation strategy targets all interested parties so that they have an opportunity to express their opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and map stakeholder categories, prioritise engagement by interest, expertise or influence, and choose methods that reach the relevant groups (research community may need specific targeting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach (minimum standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure adequate awareness-raising and publicity, and adapt communication channels to the needs of all target audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish public consultations on the 'Have Your Say' web portal as the single entry point; use the communication channels most appropriate for each target group and consider accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient time for participation (minimum standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow sufficient time for planning and responses to invitations and written contributions; as a rule, 'calls for evidence' which include public consultations are published for 12 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified minimum durations (see timeframes). For very technical initiatives, targeted (shorter) consultations may be appropriate. Ensure timelines are proportionate and allow meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of contributions and results (minimum standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish contributions to public consultations on the 'Have Your Say' web portal (and if possible on DG websites) and, where applicable, publish results and summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish contributions in the language submitted; allow respondents to choose publication with personal information or anonymised; set out data handling in a privacy statement; publish minutes/speeches from events and factual summaries within 8 weeks of closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: When stakeholder consultation is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders should normally be consulted when preparing an initiative accompanied by an impact assessment; public consultation is highly recommended for evaluations of broad public interest and fitness checks; targeted consultations are appropriate for very technical initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 'back-to-back' evaluations and impact assessments, the mandatory public consultation should cover both backward- and forward-looking elements. Use judgement for technical initiatives to choose the suitable (targeted) method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory/recommended timeframes for consultations and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified minimum durations for internet-based consultations and feedback depending on initiative type (e.g., minimum 12 weeks for initiatives with impact assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxed timeframes include: mandatory internet-based public consultation (minimum 12 weeks) for initiatives with impact assessments, back-to-back evaluations/impact assessments, consultative communications, and green papers; recommended minimum 12 weeks for evaluations of broad public interest and fitness checks; 4 weeks for 'call for evidence' documents when not published with a public consultation; 4 weeks for draft delegated and implementing acts; 8 weeks for legislative proposals adopted by the College. Exceptional short-cuts allowed only in specific urgent cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation process phases
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation process comprises three interacting phases: (1) planning and establishing the consultation strategy; (2) conducting the consultation work; and (3) informing policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each phase includes steps (planning strategy, running activities, informing about contributions, analysing responses, preparing synopsis) that together provide a framework for high-quality, transparent stakeholder consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key elements of the consultation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation strategy must clearly set out the scope and objectives; identify all relevant stakeholders; and identify appropriate consultation activities, methods and tools, ensure accessibility and consider promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these key elements in the 'call for evidence' document. For politically important initiatives, reflect on strategy during political validation and share final strategy with the interservice group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory scope of consultations for impact assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: For initiatives accompanied by impact assessments, consultation activities must cover all elements of the impact assessment process, including: the problem to be tackled; subsidiarity and the EU dimension; available policy options and potential impacts; and, when modifying existing interventions, scope for efficiency improvements and simplification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consultation materials and questionnaires elicit evidence on these elements. When evaluations are back-to-back with impact assessments, consultations must cover both sets of elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory scope for fitness checks and evaluations of broad public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation activities must cover the five mandatory evaluation criteria: relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, coherence, and EU added value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual consultation activities may focus on some criteria only, but collectively the consultation strategy must address all five criteria as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and map stakeholder groups to determine appropriate consultation methods and tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify stakeholder categories relevant to the policy, prioritise engagement according to interest/expertise/influence and consider whom it will affect, who will implement it, and who has a stated interest. Explicitly consider the research community as a source of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation methods: public vs targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose between public consultations (broad, transparent but self-selecting) and targeted consultations (focused, tap expertise, suitable for technical subjects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the representativeness and relevance of public consultation responses (especially if low response rates or coordinated campaigns are suspected). Avoid granting privileged access to some stakeholders in targeted consultations. Method choice should reflect objectives and target groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Common tools include consultation documents, questionnaires for written consultations, and direct interactions (interviews, meetings, conferences, hearings, events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select tools that match the consultation objectives and stakeholder mapping. Test tools with representative user groups to improve clarity and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcing and communicating consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Launch and announce consultation activities on a dedicated website in a form that accounts for all target audiences, using appropriate communication channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Have Your Say' as the single entry point for public consultations and adapt channels (social media, stakeholder networks, newsletters) to reach specific audiences; ensure language versions and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running consultations and acknowledging contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate sufficient resources to reply to questions, solve technical problems and process contributions (including moderation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure staffing and technical capacity for timely responses and contribution processing; acknowledge receipt; moderate inputs where necessary and keep logs of interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and testing of consultation documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of consultation documents determines the quality of contributions received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test consultation documents (presentations, surveys, questionnaires) with groups not involved in drafting but resembling target audiences; revise for clarity, accessibility and technical accuracy before launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication options for respondents' contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents should have options regarding publication of their contributions: publication with personal information or anonymised publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out procedures for collection, handling and publication of personal data in a privacy statement on the consultation page; respect data protection rules; provide anonymisation where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual summary reporting timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 8 weeks of the closure of a public consultation it is mandatory to publish a short factual summary of the key issues raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For targeted consultation activities, publishing short factual summaries on key issues is a good practice. The 8-week timeframe is indicative for large-response consultations; legislative proposal respondent feedback is published at submission time on 'Have Your Say'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysing consultation content objectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly analyse input received; present results objectively and unbiasedly, describe respondents' profiles and record all views, including dissenting ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that consultation responses are usually not statistically representative; where representative input is needed use specific methods (e.g., Eurobarometer); assess relevance of responses and be alert to signs of coordinated campaigns; apply triangulation and sensitivity checks where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis report and feedback to stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a synopsis report at the end of consultation activities to explain how and to what extent stakeholder input has been taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the synopsis to the impact assessment or evaluation report as an annex or publish as a linked SWD; for legislative proposals include a reference to the outcome of stakeholder consultation in the explanatory memorandum; effective feedback enhances transparency, accountability and future engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and core evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation is an evidence-based assessment of whether an intervention is effective, efficient, relevant, coherent and has EU added value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should look at why outcomes occurred and, if possible, quantify how much has changed. Fitness checks assess multiple related interventions jointly and should examine coherence, synergies and inefficiencies over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes and benefits of evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluations provide timely input for decision-making, organisational learning, transparency and accountability, and efficient resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evaluation results to feed impact assessments, identify follow-up actions in annual management plans, and inform strategic planning and design of future interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When evaluations are required
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation is required before revisions of EU legislation ('evaluate first'), when demanded by the legal basis of an intervention, and as indicated in the Financial Regulation (e.g., for programmes with significant spending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan evaluations with sufficient time to meet legal reporting deadlines; normally evaluations should not be conducted until at least three years of reasonably full implementation data are available, where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedural arrangements and scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation work is led by the responsible DG(s), validated in Decide, and an interservice group should be set up; the Regulatory Scrutiny Board (RSB) will scrutinise selected evaluations and all fitness checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interservice group members include better regulation support units, other interested DGs and the Secretariat-General. Interservice consultation cannot be launched before the RSB issues its opinion. If the RSB opinion is negative, the lead DG may (but is not obliged to) submit a revised draft for a second opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and transparency of evaluation outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximise transparency, final evaluation reports, the 'call for evidence', related consultation documents, contractor final studies (if applicable) and RSB opinions must be published centrally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish these materials on the 'Have Your Say' web portal and contractor studies on DG websites. Feed evaluation results into annual activity reports and identify follow-up actions in management plans; transmit summaries to EP and Council where legally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation quality principles
rubrics_metrics.description: All evaluations should be high quality and respect comprehensiveness, proportionality, independence and objectivity, and an evidence-based approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensiveness: cover at least effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, coherence and EU added value. Proportionality: tailor scope to the intervention, time since implementation and available data. Independence & objectivity: base analysis on all relevant information and report both positive and negative elements. Evidence-based approach: use best available evidence from diverse methods (triangulation), consider bias/uncertainty and apply sensitivity/scenario analysis where needed.
